task: Review native renderer tests and CI for actual Metal execution, unavailable-device handling, and required method inventory accounting.
observations: No material enforcement defect found in the assigned scope.

StudyRendererTests.testMetalMatchesCPUOnAvailableDevice constructs MetalStudyRenderer and sends every StudyValidationFixtures fixture directly through renderValidationFixture at width 96; that path calls compute without engine CPU fallback.

App/MetalStudyRenderer.swift:59-87 allocates MTLBuffers, encodes the keyfillStudy compute pipeline, dispatches threadgroups, commits the command buffer, waits for completion, requires completed status, and reads GPU output. Shared buffer storage is not the C++ shared-host numerical harness.
StudyParityMetrics.passes explicitly requires matching unsupported counts and invalid-mask positions plus mean RGB channel error <= 1 and fractionAboveFour <= 0.005.

Three Metal-specific XCTest methods throw XCTSkip when MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice is unavailable. The general engine-frame test permits either backend, but does not replace these required Metal methods.

.github/workflows/ios-prototype.yml:268-285 rejects every skipped native test and requires exactly one passed terminal outcome for each of the three Metal-specific methods. With set -euo pipefail, failed xcodebuild also fails the step; skipped-device results therefore cannot make the required CI run successful.

.github/workflows/ios-prototype.yml:287-303 runs complete native method accounting with if: always() and separately requires a finalized xcresult bundle. scripts/native_test_shards.py discovers NativeTests recursively and accepts only one ordered started -> passed event sequence per expected method, rejecting omissions, duplicates, failures, skips and unknown events.
Portable Float32/C++ checks and Metal compiler preflight are separate workflow steps and are not substituted for actual native backend testing.
